name: Datomic
tagline: Immutable Datalog database from Nubank where every fact is timestamped and queries run in the app process.
description: Datomic stores data as immutable facts (datoms: entity, attribute, value, transaction) and never overwrites them, so any past database value can be queried with Datalog, and the full history is an ordinary query away. A single transactor serialises writes while peers cache index segments and run queries inside the application process, on top of pluggable storage such as DynamoDB, PostgreSQL or Cassandra. Nubank, which acquired Cognitect in 2020, runs it at large scale and made the Datomic binaries free under Apache-2.0 in 2023. It is excellent for audit-heavy domain models in Clojure or Java, and far less common outside the JVM.

pricing.notes: Datomic Pro, Cloud and Local are free to use; you pay only for the underlying storage and compute.

scale.notes: Reads scale with peers; the single transactor caps write throughput.

strengths: Immutable facts with as-of, since and history queries built in
Datalog makes recursive and graph-style queries concise
Queries run in-process on cached indexes, scaling reads with app servers
Proven at Nubank's scale and now free to use
weaknesses: Closed source despite the Apache-2.0 binary licence
Ecosystem is largely Clojure; tooling outside the JVM is thin
Storage grows forever unless you excise data
useCases: Financial and banking domain models needing auditability
Systems that must answer what was known at a given time
Complex domain graphs in Clojure services
